guide-guardtower:
Guard Tower
Guards live and work here: one per level of the tower (one while only the tower block stands).

Main: rename the tower, choose who works here (Manage workers), call the guards back (Recall workers), and set how soon couriers come for what is in the tower's storage.
Selection tools: get a Guard Scepter. On the Guard task, right-click a block with it to make that the guards' spot. On the Patrol task, each block you click becomes the next patrol point; taking a new scepter starts the route over.
Hostiles: which creatures the guards fight. Everything is on to start with.
Settings: Guard (stay at one spot), Patrol (walk a route) or Follow (be your bodyguard, even outside the colony), and whether badly hurt guards fall back to the tower.
Minimum stock: hold an item and press Add held item; couriers keep at least that many here.
Statistics: monsters killed and more.

Guards wear armor (helmet, body, legs) from the tower's storage or the warehouse. It protects them the way it protects you and wears out.

guide-townhall:
The Town Hall is the heart of the colony. Its land protects everything around it, and its window has these tabs:

Actions: the colony's name (the pencil renames it), its numbers, and the Town Hall's own upgrade.
Quests: how far the colony's shared quests are, with a button that opens the quest book (also on the L key).
Town map: the colony from above, with the edge of its land, every building and the settlers. Scroll the mouse wheel or use + and − to zoom, drag with the mouse to move around, and point at a building to see its name.
Banners: the colony banner (from Heraldry: Banners), and buttons that copy it onto the banners of the Town Hall, the Guard Towers or every building.
Information: a log of what happened in the colony, and every work order waiting for a builder.
Citizens: Current Citizens, every living settler with their food and bed, and Dead Citizens, who died and whether they have been buried. Officers pick each settler's job here, Recall stuck ones and answer wanderers.
Statistics: settlers against beds, how many workers each job has, and what the huts have done.
Permissions: the players in the colony and their roles.
Settings: Permadeath, wanderers and the warehouse.

guide-residence:
Residence
Where families live, like MineColonies' houses. Every settler who sleeps in a bed inside the building is one of its residents.

Main: rename the Residence and order upgrades.
Residents: each household living here (a couple and their children, or someone on their own), their jobs, children's time to grow up, and whether a couple can have a child right now.

Two single adults who have lived in the colony for a couple of days pair up and move in together. A couple who are not hungry may have a child when the colony has a free bed. Children grow up into settlers who can be given a job.
citizen-no-family: No family in the colony yet.
child-no-job: Children cannot work. They grow up into settlers who can.
family-couple: {0} and {1} are now a couple and live together.
family-grown-up: {0} has grown up and can now be given a job.
family-off: Families are switched off in the config.
family-not-well: Waiting until both are well again.
family-hungry: Too hungry for a child right now.
family-enough-children: This family has all the children it wants.
family-waiting: Resting after the last child (or a new couple settling in).
family-colony-full: The colony has reached its size limit.
family-no-bed: No child until the colony has a free bed.
family-may-have-child: A child may come any day.
cmd-family-desc: Families: couple two settlers, give a couple a child, or make a child grow up (for testing).
family-cmd-notfound: No living settler named {0} in this colony.
family-cmd-cant: They cannot have a child right now: {0}
family-cmd-bad-couple: Those two cannot be a couple (one is a child, a visitor, already in a couple, or they are family).
blockdesc-waypoint-mine: For blueprints. Put it in a Miner's Hut blueprint where the top of the mine shaft goes, on the ground in the middle of the shaft. The builder leaves it out, and the miner digs its spiral staircase round it.
blockdesc-waypoint-quarry: For blueprints. Put it in a Quarry blueprint on the ground in the middle of where the pit goes. The builder leaves it out, and the quarrier digs the pit around it.
wand-tab-note-mining: The Prospector finds ore with the game's prospecting pick, the Miner digs a shaft beside its hut and goes to the ore the Prospector found, and the Quarry digs a pit for stone beside itself.
hut-placed-prospector: {0} placed. Put a prospecting pick in its storage (sneak + right-click), then give a settler the Prospector job in the Town Hall.
hut-placed-miner: {0} placed. Put a pickaxe in its storage and give a settler the Miner job. The miner digs a shaft beside the hut. Build a Prospector's Hut too, and the miner also goes to dig the good ore it finds.
hut-placed-quarry: {0} placed. Put a pickaxe in its storage and give a settler the Quarrier job. The quarrier digs a pit for stone right beside the Quarry.
hint-prospector: Put a prospecting pick in the hut's storage. The prospector wanders within {0} blocks of the hut (change this on the Work area tab), walking 25 to 50 blocks between readings, and takes a reading with the pick just as you would in density mode. It heads where the readings around look best, so it checks more near good ore and less near poor ore. Readings show on the Ore tab, on the Town Hall's Prospecting tab and on the Colony prospecting layer of your world map, and miners dig where they are best.
hint-miner: Put a pickaxe in the hut's storage, and a shovel too if you have one: soil, sand and gravel go faster with it. Put torches in too: the miner takes a few and puts one down wherever the mine gets dark, and asks couriers for more when it runs out. The miner digs a shaft beside the hut: a spiral staircase going down a level at a time, with a tunnel out from each side of every level, and it digs out any ore it sees. Upgrading the hut lets the shaft go deeper. With Go to prospected ore on (Ore tab), it first goes to good ore a Prospector found within {0} blocks, digs it out, fills the staircase back in with dirt, then comes back to the shaft. Rock and ore go into the hut's storage and couriers take them to the warehouse.
hint-quarry: Put a pickaxe in the hut's storage, and a shovel too if you have one: soil, sand and gravel go faster with it. The quarrier digs a square pit right beside the Quarry, one layer at a time, and leaves a staircase round its edge. Upgrading the Quarry makes the pit wider and deeper. The stone goes into the hut's storage and couriers take it to the warehouse.
guide-prospector:
Prospector's Hut
The prospector looks for ore with the game's prospecting pick.

Main: rename the hut, choose who works here, and order upgrades. Put a prospecting pick in the storage.
Work area: how far out the prospector goes, and whether a guard goes along.
Ore: every ore found so far, the best reading of each and where it was.

The prospector walks 25 to 50 blocks between readings, anywhere in its work area, and wears the pick down a little each time. Like a player following the pick, it heads where the readings around look best: near red (very poor) readings it rarely looks again, near yellow and green ones it looks much more. Every colony member sees the readings on the Colony prospecting layer of their world map, kept apart from their own readings.
guide-miner:
Miner's Hut
The miner digs a mine beside the hut, and goes to dig ore a Prospector found.

Main: rename the hut, choose who works here, and order upgrades. Put a pickaxe in the storage.
Work area: how far from the hut the miner may go for prospected ore, and whether a guard goes along.
Ore: turn Go to prospected ore on or off, and see the ores the colony's prospectors found. Press Mine this to go for one ore only, Any ore to let the miner pick the best reading, or New mine to start a fresh staircase there.

The shaft is a spiral staircase round a pillar of rock, so the miner can walk down and back up with what it dug. Every turn of the spiral is a level, 8 blocks deeper, with a tunnel straight out from each side. Each hut level allows two more levels. The miner digs out any ore it sees on the way. It never digs next to water or lava, into a building or into someone else's land. Bring torches if you go down to look: the mine is dark.
guide-quarry:
Quarry
The quarrier digs a pit for stone right beside the Quarry.

Main: rename the Quarry, choose who works here, and order upgrades. Put a pickaxe in the storage.
Work area: whether a guard goes along.
Quarry: where the pit is and how big it is.

The quarrier picks a side of the Quarry facing away from the Town Hall, first clears what stands above the ground there, then digs the pit a layer at a time. A staircase is left round the edge, each block one step lower than the one before. At level 1 the pit is 5 by 5 blocks and 6 deep; each upgrade makes it 2 blocks wider and 6 deeper.
workarea-range-hint-prospector: The prospector takes readings anywhere in this range, 25 to 50 blocks apart, and spends more of its time where the readings look good.
workarea-range-hint-miner: The miner only goes to readings within this range of the hut.
workstatus-needs-tool-probe: needs a prospecting pick (put one in the hut storage or the warehouse)
workstatus-needs-tool-pickaxe: needs a pickaxe (put one in the hut storage or the warehouse)
workstatus-needs-better-pick: needs a better pickaxe for the next block (put one in the hut storage)
workstatus-prospected-all: has checked the whole work area (make the Work area bigger for more)
workstatus-mine-no-readings: waiting for a Prospector to find ore
workstatus-mine-no-site: no reading in range is worth a mine (make the Work area bigger, or wait for more readings)
workstatus-mine-no-site-ore: no reading in range has the chosen ore (choose another on the Ore tab)
workstatus-mine-node-search: searching for ore close by with the prospecting pick
workstatus-mine-node-tunnel: digging a side tunnel to ore the prospecting pick found
workstatus-mine-node-ore: digging out ore the prospecting pick found
workstatus-mine-blocked: can't get to the ore that is left right now (water, a building or someone else's land is in the way)
workstatus-mine-fill-needs-dirt: needs dirt (or stone) in the hut's storage to fill in a finished mine
workstatus-mine-shaft-tunnel: digging a tunnel off the shaft
workstatus-mine-shaft-blocked: the shaft is blocked (water, lava or a building is in the way)
workstatus-mine-shaft-done: the shaft is as deep as this level of the hut allows (upgrade it to go deeper)
workstatus-mine-no-shaft-spot: no room for a shaft beside the hut (it needs land without water or other buildings, inside the colony's land)
workstatus-quarry-no-room: no room for a pit beside the Quarry (it needs flat land without water or other buildings, inside the colony's land)
workstatus-quarry-done: the pit is as deep as this level of the Quarry allows (upgrade it for a bigger pit)
workstatus-quarry-blocked: can't get to the rest of this layer right now
event-mine-done: The {0} at the reading {1} is dug out.
prospector-progress: Readings taken by the colony: {0}. About {1}% of the work area has been checked.
mine-depth: Staircase there: {0} blocks down, starting at {1}, {2}, {3}.
mine-shaft: Shaft: {0} blocks deep, level {1} of {2}, at {3}, {4}, {5}.
mine-trips-off: Go to prospected ore is off: the miner only works its shaft.
quarry-no-pit: No pit yet: the quarrier picks a spot beside the Quarry when it starts work.
quarry-pit: Pit: {0} by {0} blocks, {1} layers deep, beside the Quarry at {2}, {3}, {4}.
quarry-hint: The quarrier digs the pit one layer at a time and leaves a staircase round the edge. It never digs next to water or lava, into a building or into someone else's land. Upgrade the Quarry for a wider, deeper pit.
ore-hint-prospector: What the colony's prospectors found in {0} readings, strongest first. Each reading is also on the Colony prospecting layer of your world map.
ore-hint-miner: What the colony's prospectors found in {0} readings, strongest first.
ore-trips-hint: When on, the miner first goes to good ore the Prospector found (decent or better, or the ore you chose below), digs it out, then comes back to its shaft.
ore-none: No ore found yet. A Prospector's Hut with a prospector finds it.
skill-capped-by: Only level {0} counts here: {1} would need a higher level. Skills keep growing anyway.
skills-child: Children learn skills when they grow up.
skills-hint: Settlers learn by doing. A job skill makes that work faster; Fitness speeds up walking and adds health; Strength helps guards and couriers. A hut only lets them use as much skill as its level allows: upgrade it to use more.
cmd-skills-desc: Skills: show a settler's skills, or set one to a level (for testing).
skills-cmd-off: Skills are turned off in the config.
trait-desc-fasthealer: Back on their feet sooner, and heals quicker.
trait-desc-ironstomach: Happy to eat the same thing again.
trait-desc-patient: Waits longer before leaping to a new spot when stuck.
trait-desc-slowhealer: Stays down longer when knocked out.
trait-desc-pickyeater: Tires of the same food quickly.
trait-desc-reckless: Leaps without looking when stuck, even next to danger.
trait-desc-goodcook: Cooks fast, and knows meals a level above their skill.
trait-desc-cowardly: Runs from a fight early, and from monsters.
trait-desc-charming: Pairs up sooner, and is picked first.
trait-desc-fertile: Their couple has children more often.
trait-desc-nightowl: Sleeps midnight to 8:00; as a guard on night watch, swings faster.
trait-desc-veteran: Earned after enough kills as a guard. Kept for life.
trait-desc-shaken: Knocked out too often lately. Fades after some quiet days.
trait-idle: Does nothing in their current job ({0}).
trait-child: Starts working when they grow up.
trait-level-hint: Level {0} of 20. Traits grow a little every day, faster while in use: good ones get stronger, bad ones milder.
traits-cmd-off: Traits are turned off in the config.
traits-off: Traits are turned off in the config.
colony-full: The colony is full: upgrade the Town Hall to make room for more settlers.
tavern-population: Settlers: {0} of {1}. Each Town Hall level makes room for more.
tavern-full: Settlers: {0} of {1}. The colony is full: upgrade the Town Hall to hire more.
recruits-full: The colony is full ({0} of {1}). Upgrade the Town Hall to hire more.
citizen-traits-later: Traits are coming soon: each settler will have a few that change how they live and work.
skills-off: Skills are turned off in the config.
citizen-inventory-hint-edit: Click a slot to take an item or put the one on your cursor in, as with your own inventory. Right-click takes half or puts one; shift-click sends it to your inventory. The tool bar takes one weapon, three tools and anything in the offhand (a shield shows in the left hand). Packed food only takes food.
gear-members-only: Only colony members can take or give a settler's things.
gear-does-not-fit: {0} does not go in that slot.
activity-picking-up: Picking up items from the ground
activity-fetching-torch: Fetching a torch for the dark
activity-dropping-off: Dropping things off at the hut
questbook-pick: Click a quest on the map to read it. Drag to move the map.
questbook-needs-colony: Join or found a colony first: this quest belongs to a colony.
questbook-accept-hint: Accept this quest to start it. Dropping it later costs nothing.
quests-chapter-empty: No quests here yet. This chapter fills in a later update.
quest-ready: Quest ready to claim: {0}. Press L to open the quest book.
quest-not-available: That quest cannot be accepted right now.
quest-not-active: That quest is not in progress.
quest-not-complete: That quest is not finished yet.
townhall-quests-intro: The colony's shared quests. The Story and The Colony groups count for everyone in the colony; the other groups are each player's own.
objective-camp: Place the Supply Camp and take its kit
quest-p-camp-desc:
"So you're the one heading out to settle the valley," the Quartermaster says, pushing a crate across the counter. "Camp's in there, and everything you need to start. Set it up where you like, open it up, and take what's inside."

Place the Supply Camp and take the starting kit from it.
quest-p-ledger-desc:
"And this," the Quartermaster adds, tapping a leather-bound book, "is the ledger. Every colony keeps one. Lose it and the next one costs you leather, paper and charcoal, so keep it close."

Keep the Colony Ledger in your bag. Right-click it to open this book; sneak and right-click to open the Town Hall.
quest-p-townhall-desc:
"Find good ground: flat, near water, with trees in reach. Put the Town Hall down there and the valley is yours. Settlers follow a Town Hall, not a tent."

Place the Town Hall with the Builder's Wand to found your colony.
quest-s1-builder-desc: The Town Hall is only a flag in the mud until someone builds it. Place the Builder's Hut from the kit; the first settler to arrive will take the job.
quest-s1-first-settler-desc: A figure comes down the road with a pack on their back. The first settler of a colony is always remembered: their name goes on the first page of the ledger.
quest-s1-townhall-built-desc: The builder needs materials for the Town Hall's first level. Carry what the work order asks for to the Builder's Hut, and the colony's first real building goes up.
quest-s1-warehouse-desc: "We can't keep stacking crates in the Town Hall," the first settler says. Place a Warehouse: couriers will carry the colony's stock to it, and every hut draws from it.
quest-s1-three-desc: Word spreads. With a roof over the Town Hall and a place to store things, more settlers are willing to stay. Three settlers make a colony that will last the winter.
quest-s2-residence-desc: Settlers sleeping on the Town Hall floor grumble by morning. Place a Residence and have it built, and each of them gets a bed.
quest-s2-forester-desc: "Every plank in this place came in on your back," the first settler points out. "Give someone an axe." Place a Forester's Hut and give a settler the Forester job in the Town Hall's Citizens tab.
quest-s2-logs-desc: The forester fells, the courier carries. When logs are piling up in the Warehouse, the colony can build without you.
quest-s2-courier-desc: Someone has to walk the loads from the huts to the Warehouse. Give a settler the Courier job.
quest-s2-five-desc: The trader's cart stops on its way through. "Five of you now? Last year this was a field." Five settlers, housed and working, close the second chapter.
quest-s3-farmer-desc: Bread does not grow on its own. Place a Farmer's Hut, mark a field, and give a settler the Farmer job.
quest-s3-grain-desc: The farmer's first harvest goes into the Warehouse. When the grain is in, the colony eats from its own fields.
quest-s3-cook-desc: Raw grain and a hungry settler make a poor evening. Place a Cook's Hut and give a settler the Cook job; the cook feeds everyone from the Warehouse's stores.
quest-s3-potter-desc: "If I have to shape one more pot by hand..." Place a Potter's Hut and give a settler the Potter job; they turn clay into the vessels the kitchen needs.
quest-s3-eight-desc: The cook serves eight bowls a night now. The first settler says it quietly over supper: "This is a village."
quest-s4-tavern-desc: The trader has a warning with the news this time: "Bandits on the north road. They're watching the villages that grow." Build a Tavern: travellers bring news, and some stay.
quest-s4-hold-desc: "We dig in," says the first settler. "Walls, a tower, and guards who know the ground." Build a Guard Tower and give two settlers the Guard job.
quest-s4-roads-desc: "We make friends," says the trader. "A village with many hands is a poor target." Welcome three wanderers who ask to join, and bring another player into the colony.
quest-s4-twelve-desc: Twelve settlers, a tavern full of talk, and smoke from twelve chimneys on a cold morning. Whatever path you chose, the valley is a real village now.
quest-s5-couples-desc: Settlers who share a Residence long enough become couples. Two couples in the colony mean children are not far behind.
quest-s5-child-desc: The ledger gets a new kind of entry: a birth. The first child born in the colony carries its name.
quest-s5-ten-buildings-desc: Ten buildings, each with its work. The trader no longer calls it a village.
quest-s5-townhall-3-desc: Bring the Town Hall to level 3. The bandit leader's scouts have been seen on the ridge; a town with a proper hall is one they think twice about.
quest-s5-twenty-desc: Twenty settlers. The first settler, grey now at the temples, reads the ledger's first page aloud at supper, and the hall goes quiet.
quest-s6-tower-2-desc: The bandit leader sends a message by the trader: "Tell them to leave the gates open." Bring the Guard Tower to level 2.
quest-s6-guards-desc: Four guards walk the patrol points through the night. Give four settlers the Guard job.
quest-s6-kills-desc: The guards prove themselves against whatever comes out of the dark. Ten kills in the colony's defence.
quest-s6-townhall-4-desc: With the walls manned and the hall at level 4, the colony is ready for whatever the north road brings. Raids themselves arrive in a later update; this chapter's reward waits for you now.
quest-age-knife-desc: Knap a knife from flint or stone. It cuts grass, skins animals and opens the world's first recipes.
quest-age-axe-desc: Knap an axe and fell your first tree.
quest-age-sticks-desc: Gather sticks from the ground and dry grass from the tall grass: the stuff of fire pits and beds.
quest-age-fire-desc: Carry firewood: a fire pit cooks food and keeps the dark a little further off.
quest-age-spear-desc: A flint spear keeps wolves at the length of a stick.
quest-age-camp-desc: Place the Supply Camp and take the colony's starting kit: this is where the Story begins.
quest-age-clay-desc: Find clay near water and dig it out. Everything in this chapter is shaped from it.
quest-age-bowl-desc: Shape a bowl from clay and fire it in a pit kiln.
quest-age-pot-desc: Shape a cooking pot and fire it: stews feed better than anything roasted on a stick.
quest-age-vessels-desc: Fire four storage vessels. Vegetables keep for months in them.
quest-age-crucible-desc: Shape and fire a crucible. It is the door to the Copper Age.
quest-age-potter-desc: Place a Potter's Hut and give a settler the Potter job, so the colony shapes its own clay.
quest-age-copper-ore-desc: Find native copper or malachite on the surface or in caves, and bring back eight pieces of ore.
quest-age-charcoal-desc: Build a charcoal pit from firewood, seal it, and light it. Charcoal burns hot enough to melt copper.
quest-age-molds-desc: Shape and fire an ingot mold and two tool molds.
quest-age-copper-ingots-desc: Melt copper in a crucible over a fire pit and pour four ingots.
quest-age-copper-pick-desc: Cast a copper pickaxe: stone and ore come loose for it that flint never touched.
quest-age-builder-2-desc: Bring the Builder's Hut to level 2. A better hut means bigger work orders.
quest-age-tin-ore-desc: Copper alone is soft. Find cassiterite or bismuthinite ore to alloy with it.
quest-age-bronze-desc: Mix copper and tin in a crucible and cast eight bronze ingots.
quest-age-anvil-desc: Cast a bronze anvil. From here on, tools are hammered, not poured.
quest-age-hammer-desc: Make a bronze hammer and a bronze pickaxe.
quest-age-propick-desc: Make a prospecting pick. It tells you what ores lie under your feet, and the colony's Prospector uses one too.
quest-age-guards-desc: Give two settlers the Guard job and put bronze in their hands.
quest-age-bloomery-desc: Build a bloomery from fire bricks. Iron does not melt in a crucible.
quest-age-bloom-desc: Smelt iron ore in the bloomery and pull out an iron bloom.
quest-age-iron-ingots-desc: Hammer the bloom into iron ingots on the anvil.
quest-age-forge-desc: Build a forge: it heats iron to working temperature where a fire pit cannot.
quest-age-tower-desc: Build a Guard Tower and have it finished.
quest-age-blister-desc: Pack iron ingots with charcoal in a cementation furnace and bake them into blister steel.
quest-age-steel-desc: Refine blister steel into steel ingots.
quest-age-steel-pick-desc: Forge a steel tool. Nothing in the ground resists it.
quest-age-townhall-4-desc: Bring the Town Hall to level 4, the mark of a colony that has come through every age.
quest-c-townhall-desc: Use the Builder's Wand to place the Town Hall. The land around it becomes the colony's.
quest-c-townhall-1-desc: The Town Hall starts as a marker. Place a Builder's Hut and have the Town Hall's first level built.
quest-c-name-desc: Open the Town Hall window (sneak and right-click the Ledger, or right-click the Town Hall) and give the colony a name with the pencil on the Actions tab.
quest-c-builder-hut-desc: Place the Builder's Hut from the Supply Camp kit. Every building in the colony goes through it.
quest-c-builder-job-desc: Give a settler the Builder job in the Town Hall's Citizens tab.
quest-c-builder-2-desc: Order the Builder's Hut's second level from its window, carry the materials in, and watch it go up.
quest-c-two-desc: Settlers wander in when the colony has beds and a Town Hall. Keep two.
quest-c-jobs-desc: Give every job a hut and every settler a job: at least one Builder and one Courier.
quest-c-four-desc: A colony of four, each with a job.
quest-c-warehouse-desc: Place a Warehouse. Its chests hold the colony's stock, and every hut takes and gives from it.
quest-c-courier-desc: Give a settler the Courier job; they carry from the huts and the drop-off to the Warehouse.
quest-c-stock-desc: Two hundred items of anything in the colony's storage.
quest-c-farmer-desc: Place a Farmer's Hut, mark a field with its markers, and give a settler the Farmer job.
quest-c-cook-desc: Place a Cook's Hut and give a settler the Cook job. Hungry settlers go to the cook for meals.
quest-c-bread-desc: Eight loaves in the colony's storage, ready for hungry settlers.
quest-c-residence-desc: Place a Residence and have it built. Settlers who live together may become a couple.
quest-c-couple-desc: Two settlers who share a Residence become a couple in time.
quest-c-born-desc: A child is born to a couple with room in their Residence.
quest-c-grown-desc: A child grows up and takes a job of their own.
quest-c-tower-desc: Place a Guard Tower and have it built.
quest-c-guard-desc: Give a settler the Guard job and a weapon from the tower's window.
quest-c-patrol-desc: Guards visit patrol points through the night. Twenty visits.
quest-c-kills-desc: The guards kill five things that came for the colony.
quest-c-banner-desc: With Heraldry: Banners installed, set a colony banner on the Town Hall's Banners tab.
quest-h-grass-desc: Cut tall grass with a knife and gather dry grass for a bed and thatch.
quest-h-logs-desc: Fell trees and stack eight logs.
quest-h-bed-desc: Make a bed: the night passes faster lying down.
quest-h-firewood-desc: Split logs into firewood with an axe.
quest-h-torches-desc: Light four torches from a fire pit and set them around camp.
quest-h-lantern-desc: Make a lantern: light that does not burn out.
quest-h-bowls-desc: Fire four bowls to eat from.
quest-h-cooked-desc: Cook meat or vegetables over a fire pit.
quest-h-grain-desc: Harvest grain from wild or farmed crops.
quest-h-flour-desc: Grind grain into flour in a quern.
quest-h-dough-desc: Mix flour and water into dough.
quest-h-bread-desc: Bake eight loaves in a clay oven.
quest-h-vessel-desc: Fire storage vessels: vegetables and grain keep far longer in them.
quest-h-barrel-desc: Make a barrel for brining and pickling.
quest-h-pickles-desc: Pickle vegetables in a barrel of brine.
quest-h-bucket-desc: Make a wooden bucket for milk.
quest-h-cheese-desc: Curdle milk and age a wheel of cheese.
quest-h-juice-desc: Press fruit into juice in a barrel and let it ferment.
quest-l-berries-desc: Pick sixteen berries or other fruit from bushes and trees.
quest-l-mushrooms-desc: Gather eight mushrooms. Learn which ones not to eat.
quest-l-cattails-desc: Dig cattail roots from the water's edge.
quest-l-forester-desc: Place a Forester's Hut and give a settler the Forester job.
quest-l-hoe-desc: Make a hoe to till soil.
quest-l-farmer-desc: Place a Farmer's Hut, mark a field, and give a settler the Farmer job.
quest-l-cutting-desc: Take a cutting from a fruit tree with shears or a knife.
quest-l-orchard-desc: Pick thirty-two fruit from your own trees.
quest-l-hides-desc: Skin four animals for their hides.
quest-l-meat-desc: Bring home eight pieces of raw meat.
quest-l-skep-desc: Weave a skep from dry grass and set it near flowers.
quest-l-honey-desc: Harvest honeycomb and press it into honey.
quest-l-larder-desc: Sixty-four vegetables or grain stored for the cold months.
quest-l-propick-desc: Cast or forge a prospecting pick.
quest-l-prospector-desc: Place a Prospector's Hut and give a settler the Prospector job; they take readings around the colony.
quest-l-readings-desc: The colony's prospectors take ten readings.
quest-l-ore-desc: Mine thirty-two ore of any kind.
quest-l-miner-desc: Place a Miner's Hut and give a settler the Miner job; they dig out the ores the prospector found.
quest-l-quarry-desc: Place a Quarry and give a settler the Quarrier job for stone.
quest-l-dug-desc: The colony's miners and quarriers dig a hundred blocks.
quest-k-spear-desc: Knap a spear head and haft it.
quest-k-arrows-desc: Knap eight arrowheads and fletch them.
quest-k-door-desc: Make a door for your house.
quest-k-leather-desc: Tan hides into leather: a long job of lime, water and time.
quest-k-glass-desc: Melt sand and quartz into glass.
quest-k-windmill-desc: Make a windmill rotor and let the wind do the grinding.
quest-t-cobble-desc: Thirty-two cobblestone or stone bricks for a road out of the mud.
quest-t-waypoint-desc: Place a colony Waypoint on the road so settlers path along it.
quest-t-gears-desc: Traders deal in rusty gears. Gather five.
quest-t-raft-desc: Build a raft or boat and take to the water.
quest-t-temporal-desc: A temporal gear repairs a translocator. Find one.
quest-d-light-desc: Keep torches to hand: drifters come where it is dark.
quest-d-guards-desc: The colony's guards kill ten drifters.
quest-d-gear-desc: Hold a temporal gear: it steadies you when the world flickers.
quest-d-wolf-desc: Bring back hides and meat from the wild.
quest-o-rusty-desc: Ruins leave rusty gears behind. Find one.
quest-o-book-desc: Find a book left by those who came before.
workstatus-needs-tool-hammer: needs a hammer (put one in the hut storage or the warehouse)
hut-placed-smelter: {0} placed. Right-click it to order level 1 (it comes with a fire pit), give a settler the Smelter job in the Town Hall, and put nuggets, charcoal, a fired crucible and fired ingot molds in the hut's storage (sneak + right-click).
hut-placed-blacksmith: {0} placed. Right-click it to order level 1 (it comes with a forge), put an anvil next to it, give a settler the Blacksmith job in the Town Hall, and put a hammer, ingots, charcoal and sticks in the hut's storage (sneak + right-click).
hint-smelter: Put nuggets (or metal bits), charcoal, a fired crucible and fired ingot molds in the hut's storage; couriers bring them from the warehouse too. The smelter sets the molds out beside the fire pit, fills the crucible with one kind of nugget, puts it on the fire with charcoal and pours the metal into the molds once it has melted, just as you would. It takes the ingots out when they have cooled. Copper needs charcoal or coal: firewood is not hot enough. The Smelting tab says how many ingots of each metal to keep.
hint-blacksmith: Put a hammer, ingots, charcoal and sticks in the hut's storage; couriers bring them from the warehouse too. The blacksmith needs the game's forge and an anvil within 8 blocks of the hut. It heats the ingots in the forge, hammers them into the piece on the anvil, and puts tool heads on a stick to make the finished tool. The anvil must be good enough for the metal, as for you. The Smithing tab says how many of each thing to keep.
guide-smelter:
Smelter's Hut
The smelter melts nuggets into ingots with the game's fire pit, crucible and ingot molds.

Main: rename the hut, choose who works here, and order upgrades. Put nuggets, charcoal, a fired crucible and fired ingot molds in the storage.
Smelting: every metal the game melts in a crucible, how many ingots the colony has, and how many to keep. The smelter only works on metals you keep some of.

The smelter keeps up to 4 molds set out beside the fire pit and melts up to 4 ingots at a time, one kind of nugget per crucible (no bronze yet). Copper melts at about 1084 degrees, so it needs charcoal or coal; tin and lead melt with firewood.
guide-blacksmith:
Blacksmith's Hut
The blacksmith makes tool heads, tools and other metal pieces from ingots, with the game's forge and anvil.

Main: rename the hut, choose who works here, and order upgrades. Put a hammer, ingots, charcoal and sticks in the storage.
Smithing: everything the game's smithing recipes make from the metals the colony has ingots of, with how many ingots each takes. Set how many to keep; the blacksmith only makes what you keep some of.

The blacksmith does not move voxels one by one like you do: it strikes the anvil a number of times that grows with the size of the piece, and its Smithing skill makes the work faster. A tool head is put on a stick, so the colony gets the finished tool. Place an anvil within 8 blocks of the hut; a copper anvil works copper, bronze anvils work bronze, and so on.
smelting-hint: The smelter melts ingots until the colony has this many of each metal, counting the warehouse, this hut and the molds. The second number is how many nuggets make one ingot.
smelting-none: The game has no metals that melt in a crucible.
smithing-hint: The blacksmith makes pieces until the colony has this many of each, counting the warehouse and this hut. Only metals the colony has ingots of are shown, and only what the anvil by the hut can work.
smithing-none: Nothing to show yet: put some ingots in the warehouse or this hut's storage.
